glossa.text:
*Let him now say.* ((ID.)) As I admonish you, so do you admonish one another; or, *let him say,* that is, let him confess.

*Because for ever.* Behold four verses of one ending.

notes.text: To Bethphage and Bethany, at the Mount of Olives — The limits of Bethany reached to the Mount of Olives, and joined to those of Bethphage. Bethphage was part of the suburbs of Jerusalem, and reached from the Mount of Olives to the walls of the city. Our Lord was now come to the place where the boundaries of Bethany and Bethphage met. Matt. xxi, 1; Luke xix, 29; John xii, 12.

glossa.text: *Of Bethany. ((BEDA.))* Bethany is a village or city on the side of Mount Olivet, etc., *as far as* two, for the knowledge of the truth and the cleanness of the work. *Two of the disciples. ((HIER.))* Two by two they are called, two by two they are sent, etc., *as far as* they may know the Lord between the two cherubim, singing with the spirit, with the mind.
*And straightway. ((BEDA.))* The preachers, entering the world, found the people of the nations, etc., *as far as* but that which is clean and holy belongs to God alone.

*A colt tied. ((HIER.))* The colt tied and untamed, which they loose and tame, is the Gentile people. Before the door of faith it stands with the bonds of its own sins where two ways meet: in the freedom of choice it wavers between death and life.
*And they let them go. ((BEDA.))* They who at the loosing spoke against it, etc., *as far as* they cover them with that whereby, with Christ as their rider, they may be made worthy.
*And he sat. ((HIER.))* He began to reign, that sin might not reign in mortal or in wanton flesh: but justice and peace and joy in the Holy Ghost.

*But many spread their garments.* Because many martyrs, stripping themselves of the covering of their own flesh, prepare a way with their blood for the simpler sort, that these may go unhindered to the city on high, to which Jesus leads.

*((HIER.)) Many,* etc. The feet are the outermost members, which the Apostle appointed for the joining together, which, although they are not the back on which the Lord sat, yet are instructed along with the soldiers by John.

*And others. ((ID.))* The just shall flourish as the palm tree, narrow in the roots, broad in flowers and fruits: since they are the good odour of Christ, and they strew the way of the commandments of God with good report. ((BEDA.)) And others cut down leaves or branches from the trees, who in the teaching of the truth cull out the words and sentences of the Fathers from their books. And these they lay down in the way of God, by humble preaching, before the mind of the hearer as he comes.

*And they that went before.* The Jewish people went before, the Gentile followed. And because all who are or have been faithful believed and believe in Christ, both they who go before and they who follow cry hosanna: which in Latin is rendered, Save us: for from him also all the former sought salvation.

*Blessed is he that cometh.* Since there is one faith, one hope of all. They looked for him and believed that he would come, and we believe that he has come.

((BEDA.)) By this which is joined to it: hosanna in the highest: which is salvation, it signifies that the coming of Christ is the salvation not of men only, but of the whole world, joining earthly things to heavenly, that *to him every knee should bow, of those that are in heaven, on earth and under the earth ((Philip. II))*.

((HIER.)) This is in accord with Gabriel: who says: *He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Most High,* etc., *as far as* through the word itself of entreaty.

*And he entered in. ((ID.))* Now, the passion drawing near, he wills to be in the place appointed for the passion before the ages, etc., *as far as* he has already begun the sacrament of the blessed immolation.

*Into the temple.* He gave us an example, that wheresoever we should come, we should first turn aside to the house of prayer if there be one there: and when by the practice of prayer we have commended ourselves to God, we should withdraw to do those things for which we came. *And having looked about,* etc. He did this not once, but through all the five days. By day he taught in the temple, by night, going out, he abode on Mount Olivet, as Luke says. For by teaching he diligently bestowed on the unbelieving the office of correction, by abiding among the faithful he graciously showed forth the grace of kindness.

*And when he had seen. ((BEDA.))* As he speaks by parables, so he does, etc., *as far as* by working miracles, and he found none: therefore he condemned it.

praise.title: O Praise Him (All This for a King)

echoes.attribution: Catena, CC BY-SA 4.0 (Wilson Pruitt / Wroot Press)

echoes.text: Rejoice greatly, daughter of Zion! Shout, daughter of Jerusalem! Behold, your King comes to you! He is righteous, and having salvation; lowly, and riding on a donkey, even on a colt, the foal of a donkey.
echoes.note: The deliberate procurement and riding of a young donkey into Jerusalem evokes Zechariah's humble king who comes 'lowly and riding on a donkey, on a colt the foal of a donkey.' Mark does not quote it (unlike Matthew/John), but the staged colt-riding has high coherence with the messianic peace-king imagery, and the theme recurs across the entry tradition. Volume is strong despite the missing citation.

echoes.text: Save us now, we beg you, Yahweh! Yahweh, we beg you, send prosperity now. Blessed is he who comes in Yahweh’s name! We have blessed you out of Yahweh’s house.
echoes.note: The crowd's cry 'Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord!' formally cites the Hallel pilgrimage acclamation, where 'Hosanna' (hoshia-na, 'save now') is Ps 118:25 and the blessing is 118:26. This is a verbatim liturgical quotation with maximal volume; the same psalm recurs as the rejected-stone text in Mark 12:10-11, strengthening recurrence.

echoes.text: Binding his foal to the vine, his donkey’s colt to the choice vine; he has washed his garments in wine, his robes in the blood of grapes.
echoes.note: Jacob's blessing of Judah, 'binding his foal to the vine and his donkey's colt to the choice vine,' supplies an old messianic-royal association of the bound colt that Second-Temple readers connected to the coming ruler of Judah (Gen 49:10). Mark's emphatically tied, never-ridden colt that is untied coheres with this figural Judahic kingship, though the link is mediated and contested.

echoes.text: Then they hurried, and took every man his garment, and put it under him on the top of the stairs, and blew the trumpet, saying, “Jehu is king.”
echoes.note: Spreading garments on the road as Jesus rides echoes the acclamation of Jehu, where the people 'took every man his garment, and put it under him... and blew the trumpet, saying, Jehu is king.' The shared royal-enthronement gesture of garments under the new king gives coherence to reading the entry as a kingmaking, though Mark adds the cut branches.

echoes.text: When your days are fulfilled, and you shall sleep with your fathers, I will set up your seed after you, who shall proceed out of your bowels, and I will establish his kingdom. He shall build a house for my name, and I will establish the throne of his kingdom forever. I will be his father, and he shall be my son. If he commits iniquity, I will chasten him with the rod of men, and with the stripes of the children of men; but my loving kindness shall not […]
echoes.note: The crowd hails 'the coming kingdom of our father David,' invoking the Davidic covenant promise of an enduring throne and kingdom for David's offspring. The Davidic-dynastic frame of the entry coheres with Nathan's oracle, the foundational text for messianic kingship, though Mark cites no words from it.

echoes.text: Lift up your heads, you gates! Be lifted up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in. Who is the King of glory? Yahweh strong and mighty, Yahweh mighty in battle. Lift up your heads, you gates; yes, lift them up, you everlasting doors, and the King of glory will come in. Who is this King of glory? Yahweh of Armies is the King of glory! Selah.
echoes.note: The king's approach to Jerusalem and entry into the temple faintly recalls the processional liturgy of the King of glory entering the gates. The coherence is thematic (royal advent into the sanctuary), but there is no verbal contact, so the echo is faint and contested.

echoes.text: His feet will stand in that day on the Mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east; and the Mount of Olives will be split in two, from east to west, making a very great valley. Half of the mountain will move toward the north, and half of it toward the south.
echoes.note: Mark situates the entry at the Mount of Olives, the very site where Zechariah says the LORD's feet will stand on the day of his eschatological coming. The geographic note may be loaded with this Day-of-the-LORD coherence, but the topographic detail is also simply realistic, so the allusion is contested.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Open to me the gates of righteousness.
This is the gate of the Lord.
Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord.
Hosanna in the highest!
They spread their cloaks and branches on the road.
Hosanna to the Son of David!
Come, let us go up with him to the city.
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Hear the crowd swell along the road, cloaks and green branches thrown down in the dust before him.
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
He rides not a warhorse but a borrowed colt, humble and lowly, a king the city never expected.
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
Open wide the gates of righteousness; the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!
So lift your branches, lift your voices, and go up with him to the holy city.
Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord! Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Branches and cloaks strew the dusty road.
Hosanna in the highest!
A humble king rides in on a borrowed colt.
Hosanna in the highest!
Open the gates; the cornerstone arrives.
Hosanna in the highest!
Come, go up with him to the city.
Hosanna in the highest! Amen.
